attack: Deliver a pull_request webhook signed with a wrong secret, a correctly signed body altered after signing, and an unsigned body
consequence: An attacker without the webhook secret cannot trigger or suppress scans
expected: All rejected before parsing; no scan, no check
limitation: A leaked webhook secret defeats this control; rotate it
mitigation: HMAC-SHA256 signature verified in constant time over the raw body
observed: HTTP 401 (wrong secret), 401 (altered body), 401 (unsigned), reasons ["{'error': 'invalid webhook signature'}", "{'error': 'invalid webhook signature'}", "{'error': 'missing webhook signature'}"]; scans processed 0; check runs before the control 0; correctly signed control: {'status': 'queued'}

attack: Redeliver an old webhook (same delivery ID), then deliver the old event again under a new delivery ID after a newer commit was scanned
consequence: A PASS for an outdated commit cannot hide a violation added later
expected: The replay is a duplicate; the late event cannot turn the pull request's newer BLOCK into a PASS
limitation: Checks are per commit SHA: an old commit's own check can still show its old result, which is correct for that SHA
mitigation: Delivery records with payload digests; check ownership per repository, SHA and check name; newest-scan-wins
observed: replay response {'status': 'duplicate'}; late event response {'status': 'duplicate'}; newest commit check still failure; old commit job states ['passed']

attack: GitHub's API is unreachable during a scan of a clean commit; separately, the installation's Checks permission is reduced to read
consequence: A required check stays unsatisfied; merges wait instead of passing unverified code
expected: Neither produces a successful check (fail closed)
limitation: Availability: while GitHub or the service is down, required checks block merging
mitigation: Bounded retries, then ERROR; never a success conclusion without a completed evaluation
observed: outage: job error (infrastructure), check conclusions []; revoked: job error (authorization), check runs 0

attack: Re-run the passing check of an outdated commit after a violating commit was pushed; queue a pull request whose own head passed while an AI-attributed change is queued ahead of it
consequence: Neither a stale re-run nor a queue candidate can inherit an earlier PASS
expected: The stale re-run is refused; the merge group commit is scanned itself and blocked
limitation: Requires the repository's merge queue to require the CommitGuard check
mitigation: Re-runs only for the newest commit of a pull request or branch; merge_group events scan base..merge-group SHA
observed: stale re-run response {'status': 'ignored'}; newest pull request check failure; pull request head check success; merge group 268db8c11243 check failure

consequence: Repository administrators cannot opt out of organization requirements
expected: Without a central floor the repository decides; with a mandatory policy the rule still blocks
limitation: Only repositories scanned by the GitHub App with the floor configured are covered; GitHub Actions uses repository configuration
mitigation: Mandatory policy floors (service policy, Phase 8 organization/group mandatory entries)
observed: without mandatory policy: success; with mandatory policy: failure

attack: The service database fails while a webhook is received
consequence: No false PASS; the event is not lost if GitHub redelivers it
expected: The webhook is answered with an error (so GitHub can redeliver); no check is reported as passing; a redelivery after recovery is processed
limitation: GitHub does not redeliver automatically: an operator must redeliver from the App's delivery log
mitigation: Event recorded before processing; errors surface as 5xx; redelivery processed
observed: HTTP 500 {"error": "internal error"}; scans processed 0; checks while down []; redelivery response {'status': 'queued'}; check after recovery success

attack: The GitHub App installation is suspended, then a pull request is opened
consequence: Enforcement stops while suspended and the dashboard shows repositories at risk instead of protected
expected: State recorded, audit event and notification created, no passing check
limitation: While suspended GitHub sends no events and no check is created; only a required check keeps merges blocked
mitigation: Installation lifecycle events, critical notification, AT RISK posture
observed: installation state suspended; scans processed 0; checks []; audit contains installation_suspended: True; notification installation_disconnected: True

attack: git commit --no-verify and git push --no-verify with an AI co-author trailer
consequence: The violating commit reaches the remote branch but cannot be merged while the check is required
expected: Local hooks are skipped; the pull request check blocks the commit
limitation: Without a required check, a --no-verify push can be merged; CommitGuard cannot configure branch protection
mitigation: Server-side check (GitHub Actions or GitHub App) required by branch protection or a ruleset
observed: normal commit exit 1; --no-verify commit exit 0; --no-verify push exit 0; pull request check exit 1 (BLOCK); modelled required-check gate allows merge: False

attack: Delete the pre-commit, commit-msg and pre-push hook files, then commit and push
consequence: Local prevention is lost silently until doctor is run
expected: Local enforcement is gone; doctor reports it; the pull request check blocks
limitation: Git gives hooks no integrity protection; a developer controls their own .git/hooks
observed: commit exit 0 (allowed); doctor exit 2, reports missing hooks: True; pull request check exit 1 (BLOCK)

attack: Edit the managed hook block so it exits 0 before running CommitGuard
consequence: Local prevention silently disabled for this clone
expected: The edited hook allows the commit; doctor flags the checksum mismatch; the pull request check blocks
limitation: A checksum detects edits only when doctor runs; it does not prevent them
mitigation: Managed-block checksum reported by commitguard doctor; server-side required check
observed: commit exit 0; doctor reports modified hooks: True; pull request check exit 1 (BLOCK)

attack: Point core.hooksPath at an empty directory; separately, commit from a fresh clone without installing hooks
consequence: Any clone without CommitGuard hooks has no local enforcement
expected: Both commits are allowed locally; both pull request checks block
limitation: Hooks are per clone and opt-in by design of Git
mitigation: Server-side required check; commitguard install --global for developer machines
observed: core.hooksPath commit exit 0; fresh clone commit exit 0; pull request checks exit 1 and 1

attack: In the pull request itself, disable ai_coauthor, set it to allow, or delete .commitguard.yaml
consequence: A pull request cannot relax the policy that evaluates it
expected: Policy is read from the pull request base; every variant is blocked
limitation: Once a relaxing change is merged into the base branch it applies to later pull requests, unless an organization mandatory policy (GitHub App) sets a floor
mitigation: Trusted policy source: the base commit (Phase 4)
observed: pull request check exit codes: disable=1, allow=1, delete=1

attack: A pull request removes or neuters the CommitGuard workflow so no check runs
consequence: Only branch protection that requires the check stops the merge; the GitHub App check does not depend on the repository's workflow files
expected: No successful required check exists, so a required-check gate refuses the merge
limitation: Modelled gate, not GitHub: verifying the real branch protection needs a GitHub repository (see docs/research/github-enforcement-validation.md)
mitigation: Require the check in branch protection or a ruleset; prefer the GitHub App, which runs outside the repository
observed: no check conclusion for c61279998f75; modelled gate allows merge: False
